props.title: Johnny Mnemonic

sections.content: Johnny Mnemonic (1995) represents cyberpunk's awkward transition to mainstream Hollywood, arriving just as the internet was becoming household technology. Based on William Gibson's 1981 short story, it stars Keanu Reeves as a data courier who stores sensitive information in his brain-implanted hard drive. While the film stumbled commercially, it eerily predicted issues we face today - corporate control of data, digital privacy, and information overload. The film shares DNA with Strange Days (1995) and Until the End of the World (1991) in exploring how digital storage of memories and experiences affects human consciousness. Hackers|1995|Teen hackers battle corporate conspiracy in this stylish cult classic featuring young Angelina Jolie|Netflix The Lawnmower Man|1992|A simple gardener becomes a digital god through virtual reality experiments|Prime Virtuosity|1995|Denzel Washington hunts a virtual reality killer who's escaped into the real world|Hulu

The mid-90s saw a wave of films grappling with emerging digital technology fears. The Net (1995) tapped into identity theft anxiety, while Virtuosity (1995) explored artificial intelligence running amok. These films often featured exaggerated representations of cyberspace - like Johnny Mnemonic's data visualization sequences - that seem quaint now but captured the period's mix of excitement and fear about digital frontiers.

Director Robert Longo brought his visual arts background to create striking cyberpunk imagery, though the execution often feels more like an MTV music video than Gibson's gritty source material. The film shares themes with later works like eXistenZ (1999) and The Thirteenth Floor (1999) about the commodification of human consciousness and memory as data. Strange Days|1995|A dealer in recorded memories uncovers a conspiracy in pre-millennium Los Angeles|Prime New Rose Hotel|1998|Another William Gibson adaptation about corporate espionage in a high-tech future|Criterion The Thirteenth Floor|1999|Reality-bending neo-noir about virtual worlds within virtual worlds|Tubi SUBHEAD: Cyberpunk Evolution & Legacy

While Johnny Mnemonic may feel dated, its themes became more relevant with films like Inception (2010) and Source Code (2011) exploring digitized consciousness with bigger budgets and more sophisticated effects. The film's data courier concept directly influenced Lucy (2014) and Transcendence (2014), though these later films moved away from cyberpunk's anti-corporate messaging toward transhuman themes.
